SEARCH
Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.p2p

Class P2pCrypto

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.p2p.P2pCrypto
public final class P2pCrypto extends Object
The AWT-free cryptographic seam of the encrypted peer-to-peer transport. Every secret operation the P2P stack performs - generating a long-term identity, agreeing on a shared key, deriving send/receive keys, sealing and opening frames, and fingerprinting a peer - lives here as pure statics over the JDK's own javax.crypto/java.security providers, so the whole contract is unit-testable headless with no display and no third-party or native library.

The primitives mirror the project's existing VaultCrypto precedent (final class, private constructor, injectable randomness) and are chosen to be conservative and standard:

  • Key agreement: X25519 elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman (KeyPairGenerator/KeyAgreement "X25519", SunEC, JDK 11+). A fresh ephemeral X25519 keypair per handshake gives forward secrecy.
  • KDF: HKDF-SHA256, implemented directly over Mac.getInstance("HmacSHA256") (RFC 5869 extract-then-expand) so no extra dependency is needed.
  • AEAD: AES-256-GCM (Cipher "AES/GCM/NoPadding", a 96-bit nonce and a 128-bit tag). GCM is authenticated, so a tampered frame never decrypts to garbage - open(byte[], javax.crypto.SecretKey, byte[]) throws an AEADBadTagException.

Nonce discipline. A long-lived AES-GCM key must never repeat a nonce. The transport therefore uses a per-direction 96-bit counter as the nonce (see counterNonce(long)): each side owns one key and one monotonically increasing counter, so a nonce is used exactly once. The JDK's own GCM provider additionally refuses to re-initialise an encryption cipher with a repeated (key, IV), which is a useful second line of defence.

Nothing here holds state or touches the filesystem; IdentityStore owns persistence and SecureChannel/NoiseXXHandshake own the protocol. The private half of a static identity key is at-rest material: it is written 0600 by IdentityStore and documented honestly as such.

    • fingerprint

      public static String fingerprint(PublicKey publicKey) throws GeneralSecurityException
      The stable, human-comparable identity of a peer: the SHA-256 fingerprint of its X25519 public key, rendered as colon-separated lower-case hex (like an SSH host-key fingerprint). Two nodes with the same fingerprint hold the same static public key, which is the basis of TOFU pinning.
      Parameters:
      publicKey - the peer's static public key (may be null)
      Returns:
      the fingerprint, or the empty string for null
      Throws:
      GeneralSecurityException - if SHA-256 is unavailable

      Returns:

    • hkdf

      public static byte[] hkdf(byte[] ikm, byte[] salt, byte[] info, int length) throws GeneralSecurityException
      HKDF-SHA256 (RFC 5869): extract a pseudorandom key from the input keying material, then expand it to length bytes bound to info. This is how the handshake turns one raw Diffie-Hellman secret into several independent, purpose-separated AES keys.
      Parameters:
      ikm - the input keying material (the DH secret), never null
      salt - the optional salt (may be null/empty, which HKDF defines as a zero-filled hash-length string)
      info - the optional context/application info (may be null/empty)
      length - the number of output bytes to produce (must be positive and at most 255 * 32)
      Returns:
      the output keying material of exactly length bytes
      Throws:
      GeneralSecurityException - if HmacSHA256 is unavailable or the requested length is out of range

    • aesKey

      public static SecretKey aesKey(byte[] material)
      Wraps raw key material as an AES SecretKey.
      Parameters:
      material - the key bytes (must be KEY_BYTES long for AES-256)
      Returns:
      the AES key, never null

    • counterNonce

      public static byte[] counterNonce(long counter)
      Encodes a per-direction message counter as a 96-bit GCM nonce: the counter occupies the low 8 bytes (big-endian) and the high 4 bytes are zero. Using a counter rather than random bytes means a nonce is never reused under the same long-lived key, which random 96-bit nonces cannot guarantee over a long session.
      Parameters:
      counter - the monotonically increasing message counter
      Returns:
      the 12-byte nonce, never null

    • readCounter

      public static long readCounter(byte[] nonce)
      Reads back the counter encoded by counterNonce(long).
      Parameters:
      nonce - the 12-byte nonce (may be null)
      Returns:
      the counter, or -1 if the nonce is not 12 bytes long

      public static byte[] seal(byte[] plaintext, SecretKey key, byte[] nonce) throws GeneralSecurityException

    • seal

      public static byte[] seal(byte[] plaintext, SecretKey key, byte[] nonce, byte[] aad) throws GeneralSecurityException
      Seals plaintext under an AES-GCM key and nonce, binding additional authenticated data (AAD) into the tag. The transport passes the frame's type byte as AAD so a CONTROL frame cannot be replayed as a DATA frame.
      Parameters:
      plaintext - the bytes to seal (may be null, treated as empty)
      key - the AES key
      nonce - the 96-bit nonce
      aad - the additional authenticated data (may be null/empty)
      Returns:
      the ciphertext with the authentication tag appended
      Throws:
      GeneralSecurityException - if sealing fails

    • open

      public static byte[] open(byte[] ciphertext, SecretKey key, byte[] nonce) throws GeneralSecurityException
      Opens ciphertext sealed by seal(byte[], SecretKey, byte[]). Because GCM is authenticated, a tampered blob or the wrong key throws rather than returning garbage.
      Parameters:
      ciphertext - the sealed bytes (tag appended)
      key - the AES key
      nonce - the nonce used when sealing
      Returns:
      the recovered plaintext
      Throws:
      GeneralSecurityException - if the tag does not verify

    • open

      public static byte[] open(byte[] ciphertext, SecretKey key, byte[] nonce, byte[] aad) throws GeneralSecurityException

      key - the AES key
